answer.evidence: radon/raw.py:72-79 `_find(tokens, token, value)` iterates `enumerate(reversed(tokens))`, compares `(token, value) == token_values[:2]`, and returns `len(tokens) - index - 1`, which maps the reversed index back to the original index of the rightmost match. If nothing matches, it raises `ValueError('(token, value) pair not found')`. Review points: `tokens` must be a sequence because `reversed()` needs `__reversed__` or `__len__`/`__getitem__`, so a generator would fail with TypeError. Slicing `[:2]` assumes tuple-like tokens with at least two fields. The ValueError message doesn't include the missing pair, so debugging is harder. The sibling `_split_tokens` (raw.py:82-93) uses the same pair-matching convention, so the two helpers should be tested together, including the absent-pair and multiple-match cases. Time in metrics.py goes to checking whether it calls into raw-token helpers and handles the ValueError, since it consumes raw analysis results. complexity.py and visitors.py are AST-based and don't use this lookup, so they get only a quick check.
